contexts.text: To satisfy the afflicted sour () = the goods of charity in general ( = to instruct in the good of faith. AC 9050:7.) (Compare AE 386:25.)
That they are averse to the goods of charity, is signified by satiety of bread ().
When I had fed them to the full they scortated () = when truths had been revealed to them, they falsified them.
Thou openest thine hand, they are satisfied with good () = that they receive the good which inflows from the Lord.
The abundance (of good and truth) is described by, they shall eat flesh and fat to satiety, and drink blood to ebriety ().
To eat and not be satisfied () = to be deprived. (Compare AE 600:13. AE 617:20.)
Blessed are they that hunger for righteousness; for they shall be tilled ().
They that were full (). Explained. AE 721:6.
To be infilled with the good of love, is meant by, satisfied with the good-pleasure of Jehovah ().
That those who are affected with truths are fully instructed, is signified by the sons are satisfied ().
That from these things there is not any spiritual nourishment, or intelligence and affection of good, is signified by, they shall not satisfy their soul, and they shall not infill their viscera ().

To be satisfied with the good of Thy house () = to be in wisdom from Divine good; and, to be satisfied with the holiness of Thy temple = to be in intelligence from Divine truth; and, from both, to enjoy heavenly joy.
Those of the Jewish Church are called full, from the fact that they had truths in abundance.
Then they were filled () = ... to the full nourishment of the soul.
